current_abs_text: document.documentElement.classList.add('js'); [2603.29108] Efficient Bilevel Optimization with KFAC-Based Hypergradients Skip to main content Search Submit Donate Log in Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search Computer Science > Machine Learning arXiv:2603.29108 (cs) [Submitted on 31 Mar 2026] Title: Efficient Bilevel Optimization with KFAC-Based Hypergradients Authors: Disen Liao , Felix Dangel , Yaoliang Yu View a PDF of the paper titled Efficient Bilevel Optimization with KFAC-Based Hypergradients, by Disen Liao and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Bilevel optimization (BO) is widely applicable to many machine learning problems. Scaling BO, however, requires repeatedly computing hypergradients, which involves solving inverse Hessian-vector products (IHVPs). In practice, these operations are often approximated using crude surrogates such as one-step gradient unrolling or identity/short Neumann expansions, which discard curvature information. We build on implicit function theorem-based algorithms and propose to incorporate Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (KFAC), yielding curvature-aware hypergradients with a better performance efficiency trade-off than Conjugate Gradient (CG) or Neumann methods and consistently outperforming unrolling. We evaluate this approach across diverse tasks, including meta-learning and AI safety problems. On models up to BERT, we show that curvature information is valuable at scale, and KFAC can provide it with only modest memory and runtime overhead. Our implementation is available at this https URL .
